items.stem: In an execution plan, what does an index seek usually indicate compared with an index or table scan?

options.text: The engine navigated directly to the matching rows using the index
options.rationale: Correct: a seek uses the index B-tree to jump to qualifying rows rather than reading everything.

options.text: The engine read every row in the table
options.rationale: That describes a scan, not a seek.

options.text: No index exists on the table
options.rationale: A seek requires a usable index.
A seek is a normal, usually efficient operator.

items.explanation: Correct: a seek uses the index B-tree to jump to qualifying rows rather than reading everything.

items.stem: Which TWO are true about SQL Server recovery models and backups? (Select TWO)

options.text: The full recovery model supports point-in-time restore via log backups
options.rationale: Correct: full recovery with log backups enables restoring to a point in time.

options.text: The simple recovery model does not allow log backups for point-in-time restore
options.rationale: Correct: simple recovery truncates the log and has no log-backup chain.

options.text: Differential backups replace the need for a full backup
options.rationale: A differential is restored on top of a full backup; it does not replace it.

options.text: Backups can only be taken while the database is offline

items.explanation: Correct: full recovery with log backups enables restoring to a point in time.

items.stem: T-SQL is a set-based language. What does that imply for how you should write most queries?

options.text: Operate on whole sets with joins and set operations rather than row-by-row loops
options.rationale: Correct: set-based queries let the optimizer work efficiently; cursors/loops are usually slower.

options.text: Always use a WHILE loop to process one row at a time
options.rationale: Row-by-row processing is typically the slow anti-pattern.

options.text: Joins should be avoided in favour of cursors
options.rationale: Joins are the set-based tool to prefer.

options.text: Set logic only works on temporary tables
options.rationale: Set logic applies to any tables.

items.explanation: Correct: set-based queries let the optimizer work efficiently; cursors/loops are usually slower.
